findings.doc_quote: Each next run is calculated from wall-clock time, not from the previous run time.
findings.explanation: The sentence is backwards. `Every` anchors on the previous logical run (`job.next_run`) and advances by whole intervals until the result is later than the current time. The current time is only used to skip missed ticks.
findings.suggested_fix: Each next run is calculated from the previous scheduled run time, not from when the handler finished.

findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/triggers.py:121-123 — `parts = at.split(":")`, `if len(parts) != 2: raise ValueError(...)`; src/hassette/scheduler/triggers.py:398 — `Daily.__init__` calls `parse_hh_mm(at, "Daily")`. Run result: `Daily(at='07:00:30')` raised `ValueError: Daily 'at' must be 'HH:MM', got '07:00:30'`
findings.explanation: `run_daily` builds `Daily(at=at)`, which accepts exactly two colon-separated fields. An `HH:MM:SS` value raises `ValueError` at the call.

findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:670-671 — `if not name: raise SchedulerNameRequiredError(callable_name(func), str(trigger))`; src/hassette/exceptions.py:704 — `class SchedulerNameRequiredError(HassetteError)`. Run result: its MRO is SchedulerNameRequiredError, HassetteError, ReconstructibleError, Exception, BaseException, object
findings.explanation: An empty name raises `SchedulerNameRequiredError`, which is not a `ValueError` subclass. `except ValueError` will not catch it.

findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:596 — `jitter: float | None = None` (same default on every `run_*` signature, e.g. scheduler.py:799); src/hassette/scheduler/classes.py:559 — `if not jitter: return fire_time`
findings.explanation: The default is `None`, not `0`. Runtime behavior is the same, because `apply_jitter` treats both as no offset.

findings.doc_quote: Overrides the app-level handler set via scheduler.set_error_handler() .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:190 — `def on_error(self, handler: "SchedulerErrorHandlerType") -> None:`. `grep -rn set_error_handler src/ docs/pages` returned no matches
findings.explanation: `Scheduler` has no `set_error_handler` method, so calling it raises `AttributeError`. The app-level handler is registered with `scheduler.on_error()`.
findings.suggested_fix: Overrides the app-level handler set via scheduler.on_error().

findings.doc_quote: Invoked on any exception, including CancelledError .
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/core/command_executor.py:352-354 — `except asyncio.CancelledError: enqueue_result_record(); raise`; src/hassette/core/command_executor.py:541 — the error handler lookup comes after `await self._execute(...)` returns in `execute_job`
findings.explanation: `CancelledError` is re-raised out of `_execute`, so `execute_job` never reaches the error handler dispatch. Cancellation does not invoke `on_error`.
findings.suggested_fix: Invoked on any exception except CancelledError.

findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/cli/__init__.py:74 — `apps_app = App(name="app", help="List and inspect apps.")`; src/hassette/cli/__init__.py:114 — `apps_app.command(cmd_app_reload, name="reload")`. The top-level registrations at __init__.py:69-99 include no `reload` command
findings.explanation: There is no top-level `hassette reload` command. The command is `hassette app reload <key>`.

findings.doc_quote: if_exists matters most in on_initialize , which re-runs on app reload
findings.code_evidence: src/hassette/core/app_lifecycle_start_stop.py:355-359 — `reload_app` runs `_stop_app_unlocked` then `_start_app_unlocked`; src/hassette/core/app_lifecycle_start_stop.py:452 — `reload_instance`'s start path calls `create_single_instance` before initializing; src/hassette/app/app.py:158 — `self.scheduler = self.add_child(Scheduler)`; src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:147 — `self._jobs_by_name = {}`; src/hassette/scheduler/scheduler.py:185-188 — `on_shutdown` calls `remove_all_jobs()`
findings.explanation: `on_initialize` does re-run on reload, but on a new `App` with a new `Scheduler` and an empty name registry, and the old scheduler's jobs are removed at shutdown. A reload therefore does not collide with the previous run's job names, even with the default `if_exists="error"`. The same premise appears in the snippet comment at line 158 and in the prose at line 160. This comes from reading the code path, not from running a reload.
findings.suggested_fix: A reload builds a new App instance with an empty scheduler, so job names from the previous run do not collide. if_exists matters when the same name is registered more than once in one instance's lifetime, such as a handler that re-registers its job.
